title: Forty-two years, 33 moments
lede: From a Dallas software dealer to an error page. Filter by thread.

events.title: Soft Warehouse is formed
events.text: The company starts in Dallas, selling software and hardware to corporate customers.

events.title: First retail store
events.text: Soft Warehouse opens its first shop.

events.title: First Computer Superstore
events.text: The large-format store that becomes the model for the chain.

events.title: Investor group buys in
events.text: A group led by Ronald N. Dubin acquires Soft Warehouse. Nathan Morton, from Home Depot, is hired as president and CEO late in the year.

events.title: Renamed CompUSA
events.text: The company drops the Soft Warehouse name.

events.title: Tandy opens Computer City
events.text: The owner of RadioShack starts its own computer superstore chain.

events.title: Initial public offering
events.text: Shares begin trading at $15, according to a reference history.

events.title: 28 stores, $823M
events.text: Net sales for the fiscal year are $822.8M. Best Buy’s for its fiscal 1992 are $929.7M.

events.title: Morton becomes chairman
events.text: Nathan Morton adds the chairman’s title, replacing Ronald Dubin.

events.title: Morton resigns
events.text: He leaves at a board meeting. James Halpin, president for six months, takes over.

events.title: A $17.0M loss
events.text: Fiscal 1994 ends with 76 stores, $2.2B in sales, a $9.9M restructuring charge and a net loss.

events.title: PCs Compleat acquired
events.text: A Massachusetts mail-order reseller, acquired in a merger to build a direct-sales business.

events.title: Peak profit
events.text: Net income of $93.9M on sales of $4.61B, with 129 stores.

events.title: Deal for Computer City
events.text: CompUSA agrees to buy the chain from Tandy for about $275M in a note and cash.

events.title: Computer City deal closes
events.text: The final price is about $175M. CompUSA will close 59 of the 96 U.S. stores.

events.title: Restructuring announced
events.text: Corporate fulfilment is outsourced to Ingram Micro. Special charges for the year reach $93.8M.

events.title: A $45.7M loss on record sales
events.text: Fiscal 1999: 211 stores, $6.32B in sales, comparable-store sales down 3.4%.

events.title: 2,200 dismissed
events.text: The in-store corporate sales force is replaced by a call centre in Dallas.

events.title: The Slim family discloses a stake
events.text: A Schedule 13D is filed for the Slim family, Grupo Carso and Grupo Sanborns.

events.title: Sold for $10.10 a share
events.text: Grupo Sanborns agrees to buy the shares it does not own. CompUSA has 217 superstores.

events.title: Tender offer expires
events.text: About 69.5 million shares are tendered, giving the buyer about 89.9%.

events.title: Off the public record
events.text: CompUSA files a Form 15 to end its SEC reporting.

events.title: Jury verdict in Dallas
events.text: A jury finds against CompUSA, James Halpin and Slim’s companies in a suit over franchised stores in Mexico. The judge sets aside the awards against CompUSA and Halpin in May.

events.title: Good Guys bought
events.text: CompUSA agrees to pay $2.05 a share for the West Coast electronics chain.

events.title: Verdict overturned
events.text: The Dallas Court of Appeals rules that the plaintiff should take nothing from any defendant.

events.title: 126 stores to close
events.text: More than half the chain, within 90 days. 103 stores remain.

events.title: Sold to Gordon Brothers
events.text: The company says it will close its stores after the holidays. Terms are not disclosed.

events.title: Systemax buys the name
events.text: The owner of TigerDirect agrees to buy the brand, the website and up to 16 stores.

events.title: Web business changes hands
events.text: Systemax completes the purchase of the e-commerce business for $18.9M. The store leases follow in February and March.

events.title: Brand retired
events.text: Systemax consolidates its U.S. consumer business under TigerDirect and writes off the CompUSA intangibles.

events.title: A deals site borrows the name
events.text: DealCentral relaunches compusa.com as a coupon and deals page.

events.title: An error page
events.text: compusa.com returns a Wix error page for a domain that is not connected to a site.
